highlights: A broad sell-off on 18 Nov going by the heat map: almost every large share fell, led by banks (Commercial Bank −2.85%, Sampath −1.64%, HNB −1.19%, DFCC −2.04%) and diversified financials (LOLC Finance −2.04%, LFIN −3.44%, People's Leasing −3.23%, LOLC −1.43%). No ASPI figure was posted.

Other heavyweights analysed on this site also slipped: JKH −1.58%, Dialog −1.01%, Hemas −2.44%, ACL −2.77%, Royal Ceramics −2.35%, Hayleys −0.21%; only a few rose (Richard Pieris +1.10%, Capital Alliance +0.76%, CTC +0.19%, Lion Brewery +0.12%, PKME +0.15%).

Cargills Ceylon's Deputy Chairman/Group CEO Ranjit Page sold about 7mn more shares at Rs 637 (Rs 4.45bn) on 16 Nov, after selling 6mn at Rs 700 in August; his stake had already fallen from 7.9% at end-June to 5% at end-September.

The Inland Revenue Department passed its 2026 revenue target, collecting Rs 2,441.9bn by 16 Nov against Rs 2,402bn, while Cabinet approved nearly Rs 500bn of infrastructure projects amid criticism of unspent capital budgets.
Global shares fell again on 17 Nov as the AI trade unwound (Dow −1.64%, S&P 500 −1.03%, Euro Stoxx 50 −2.15%, DAX −2.08%), with the dollar near a 19-month high on expectations of a US rate hike.

news.title: IRD beats its 2026 revenue target
news.text: The Inland Revenue Department collected Rs 2,441.9bn by 16 November against a full-year target of Rs 2,402bn. It said collections for the period were Rs 491bn, 115% more than a year earlier.

news.title: Cabinet approves about Rs 500bn of projects
news.text: Projects worth nearly Rs 500bn were approved, including Rs 251.4bn for the road section of phase one of the Ruwanpura Expressway (Kahatuduwa to Ingiriya, with the system interchange). It comes amid criticism that 2026 capital spending allocations have gone unspent.

news.title: SLT-Mobitel pushes into AI, 5G and data centres
news.text: After strong profit growth in the first nine months of 2026, the state-run group is shifting from a traditional telecom operator towards a technology company, focusing on AI, targeted 5G roll-out and data centres to counter competition from global OTT platforms.

news.title: LAUGFS reverses its gas price rise
news.text: After raising prices from 13 November, LAUGFS Gas cut them on 17 November at the Trade Minister's request: the 12.5kg cylinder fell Rs 745 to Rs 5,995 and the 5kg cylinder to Rs 2,398.

news.title: Ranjit Page sells more Cargills Ceylon shares
news.text: The Deputy Chairman/Group CEO sold nearly 7mn shares at Rs 637 each (Rs 4.45bn) on 16 November, following 6mn sold at Rs 700 in August. His holding was 20.38mn shares (7.9%) at end-June and 13mn (5%) at end-September.

news.title: Dollar near a 19-month high
news.text: US retail sales rose moderately in October and Fed officials sounded hawkish, strengthening expectations of a US rate rise next month. The yen eased despite record Japanese exports in October, and the Australian dollar was near a 10-month low.

news.title: Global markets: AI trade unwind continues
news.text: World shares fell on 17 November ahead of Nvidia's results (which beat expectations) and Anthropic's market debut later in the week. On Bloomberg's screen: Dow −1.64%, S&P 500 −1.03%, FTSE 100 −1.76%, Euro Stoxx 50 −2.15%, DAX −2.08%, Nikkei −0.28%, Hang Seng −0.97%, Nifty +0.38%, KOSPI +0.63%.
